### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-flow.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via objectstack.config.js (literal, a string literal in CONFIG_FILE_CANDIDATES; a string literal in resolveConfigPath), objectstack.config.mjs (literal, a string literal in CONFIG_FILE_CANDIDATES; a string literal in resolveConfigPath), os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via objectstack.config.js (literal, a string literal in CONFIG_FILE_CANDIDATES; a string literal in resolveConfigPath))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via os generate (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 35 pages)`, `objectstack.config.ts (literal, 32 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 585c9af587a165c066c7815185a6652c2b9c545e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `baa6bf5d19c6f5fc280e2b82a6a8c3c9ffa721e5` — the merge of head `077b4c245ac84f8da1bfb8c742817c9a7f6976f7` into base `585c9af587a165c066c7815185a6652c2b9c545e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin baa6bf5d19c6f5fc280e2b82a6a8c3c9ffa721e5 && git checkout baa6bf5d19c6f5fc280e2b82a6a8c3c9ffa721e5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 585c9af587a165c066c7815185a6652c2b9c545e 077b4c245ac84f8da1bfb8c742817c9a7f6976f7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 585c9af587a165c066c7815185a6652c2b9c545e && git merge --no-ff 077b4c245ac84f8da1bfb8c742817c9a7f6976f7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 585c9af587a165c066c7815185a6652c2b9c545e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 585c9af587a165c066c7815185a6652c2b9c545e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `018fbb2ffd65b4a6e8189d9552a93c3b6c063d20`

### ① Derived judgments

- **Generated set validates in a namespaced `os init -t app` project.** `objectNameFor` (`packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts`) feeds all five object refs: `object.name`, `view.object`, `action.objectName`, flow start `config.objectName`, app nav `objectName`; the five non-object own `name`s and the action's flow `target` stay `toSnakeCase(name)`. `validateNamespacePrefix` (`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts:1766`) iterates only `config.objects`, so nothing is prefixed that the gate does not require. Unit file composes all 7 scaffolds into one namespaced stack and runs real `defineStack` plus `runAuthoringRules` with a control leg refusing pre-fix output by `STACK_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_INVALID`/422. Correct. Caveat measured by the PR itself: the init config imports only `./src/objects`, so view/action/flow/app scaffolds reach no stack until wired, and the flow needs host `requires: ['triggers']`.
- **`sys_*`, pre-prefixed, name equal to namespace, charset.** `validateObjectNamespacePrefix` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts:28`) exempts `sys_*` and accepts `startsWith(namespace + '_')`, so `my_app_invoice` is not doubled (e2e-pinned) and `os g object my_app` becomes `my_app_my_app`, which is the gate's own prescription. `ObjectSchema.shape.name` is `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` (`object.zod.ts:1608`), so `toSnakeCase` is a no-op on any accepted name; `manifest.namespace` is `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,19}$` (`manifest.zod.ts:402`) and is never passed through `toSnakeCase`. Correct. `sys_*` and name-equals-namespace are claimed in PR body and changeset but pinned nowhere.
- **One namespace source.** `readProjectNamespace` (`packages/cli/src/utils/project-namespace.ts`) calls `findConfigPath` (same `CONFIG_FILE_CANDIDATES` `resolveConfigPath` uses) then `loadConfig`, and reads `manifest.namespace` off the evaluated stack, the same object `defineStack` handed to `validateNamespacePrefix`. `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId` is not used by `defineStack`; it is used only by the runtime publish path (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:22833`), a pre-existing divergence between the two gates, not introduced here. No-config → `no-config` → no prefix; loaded without namespace → no prefix; a `packages[]`/`composeStacks` stack is read at top-level `manifest.namespace`, which is the only value the gate judges `objects` against; an array default export reads as no namespace, and `os validate` refuses that shape anyway. Load failure → `load-failed` → refusal. Nothing is written before either refusal: both sit above `generator.generate`, the parse check, the dry-run branch and `fs.writeFileSync`. Correct.
- **`loadConfig` side effect and cost.** For `object`/`view`/`action`/`flow`/`app`, every `os g` (including `--dry-run`) now runs `bundleRequire` and evaluates the whole config module with strict `defineStack` (schema parse, capability, cross-reference, namespace validators). In a `create-objectstack` blank project that module also instantiates `ConnectorRestPlugin`, `ConnectorOpenApiPlugin`, `ConnectorMcpPlugin` at evaluation. Loader stderr advisories (shadowed named exports) now print on `os g`. `dashboard`/`skill` (`namesObject: false`) never load; a broken config does not block them. A config that fails for any reason (an unrelated syntax error, a pre-fix unprefixed object, a cross-reference error) now blocks the five object-naming generators with exit 1 and the hint to run `os validate`. Documented in changeset and `cli.mdx`; it is a real cost and a new refusal.
- **Legacy `NS__SHORT` refusal.** `order__line` passes the charset gate, so the branch is reachable. Refusing in the gate's own words rather than rewriting to `my_app_line` is consistent with `#16726` option A (gate, no sanitiser, recorded in `nameCharsetRefusal`'s docblock) and with the gate. It is a NEW refusal on the published `os g` surface, but only under a namespace, where the written file was already refused by the platform's next gate. Repo precedent `.changeset/15293-non-array-packages-refusal.md` grades a refusal moved earlier as `Clause-②: no`, `patch`.
- **Prefixing explicit input vs #10712.** `applyNamespacePrefix` (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts:306`) prefixes only names the service DERIVES and REFUSES an explicit `opts.name` override. This PR applies the derived-path treatment to the author's typed name. Defensible because the typed name is the short name, the derivation is announced on stdout (`Object:` line), `os init`'s own template writes `${namespace}_item`, and triage directed exactly this. Recorded as a reading, not a defect.
- **`Args.type` help.** `Object.keys(GENERATORS).join(', ')` yields the seven metadata types; the old six-type literal appears nowhere else in the tree (`git grep` empty). `RETIRED_GENERATORS` and the four non-metadata sub-generators are still unlisted; pre-existing. Correct.
- **`cli.mdx` and changeset.** Every sentence checked against head code holds: prefix on object refs only, no doubling, loaded-config source, load-failed refusal, no prefix without namespace, `Object:` printed, "What it does" step 1. The fixture callout's `my_app_customer` becomes true: the blank starter declares `namespace: 'blank'`, rewritten to `my_app` by `create-objectstack`. Two imprecisions: `cli.mdx` says "every object name ... starts with `<namespace>_`" (omits `sys_*`, which the changeset does state) and names only `objectstack.config.ts` though `.js`/`.mjs` are read too.
- **Duplicate-name edge.** `os g object my_app_order_line` then `os g object order_line` now produce two files with the same object name; the file-exists check is by filename only and `os g` does not detect it. Outcome before and after is an `os validate` refusal, so no regression, but the failure mode moved from prefix error to duplicate.

### ② Semver level

`patch` and `Clause-②: no` are right. No public surface enlarges: `@objectstack/cli` exports only `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, and `src/index.ts` re-exports neither `utils/config.js` nor `utils/project-namespace.js`, so `findConfigPath`/`readProjectNamespace` are internal. The accept set does not widen; it narrows on two inputs, both stated in the changeset with the fix line: the legacy form under a namespace (already refused downstream, precedent 15293) and a config that exists but does not load (the platform's every other command already refuses that project). The PR body's sentence "no published accept set moves" is wrong as stated; the declaration line the gates read is still correct. A bug fix in a released package takes `patch` per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Test-tier placement: not every pinned behaviour has a per-PR pin.** `.e2e.test.ts` leaves the per-PR run (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` nightly-tiers section, `OS_TEST_TIERS`). The unit file pins templates, composed `defineStack`, control, no-namespace, pre-prefixed, and `readProjectNamespace`'s four return values. It does NOT pin: the legacy-form residual refusal in `runMetadataGeneration`; the load-failed branch refusing and writing nothing (unit pins only the reader's return value, not the command's use of it); the `Object:` stdout line; the real `os init` → `os g` → `os validate` chain. The PR's own ablation proves the gap: leg B (residual refusal disarmed) failed only in e2e. Repo convention for `os g` refusals is per-PR integration-tier spawn pins (`generate-refuses-*.test.ts`, which this PR ran green).
- **PR body claims.** Before/after, census table, one-source, no-double, `sys_*` exemption, filename/binding unchanged, help string, docs: all verified against head. "No published accept set moves": wrong as stated (two narrowings). Test counts, gate union and ablation figures not re-run; CI stands in for the tiers.
- **CI on the head** (check-runs API, last poll): 35 runs, 32 success, 2 skipped (Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 1 in_progress (the `Test Core` aggregate; all six shards, Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check workspace/debt ledger/consumer gates, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Verify CLI and Dogfood Regression 1-3 completed success), 0 failure.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20197-generate-object-namespace-prefix`
Reviewed-by: `session_01UYBdGBzWSrAMzpW8ah3GbP`

Independence: INDEPENDENT AGENT (fed the card, the rulings and the PR only; not the dispatch order or the seat's conclusions)

**VERDICT: FAIL**
- Give the two new refusals a per-PR pin: the legacy `NS__SHORT` residual refusal and the load-failed refusal (exit 1, no object file, barrel untouched) in `runMetadataGeneration` are pinned only in the nightly `generate-object-namespace-prefix.e2e.test.ts`; add them to a per-PR tier file (an integration-tier spawn pin in the `generate-refuses-*` convention, or a unit-tier pin of the command branch), so that disarming either branch reds the PR run rather than the next nightly on `main`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `077b4c245ac84f8da1bfb8c742817c9a7f6976f7`

Delta of: `5855043147` (FAIL on `018fbb2f`)

### ① Derived judgments

- **Required change: both refusal branches now have a per-PR pin.** New file `packages/cli/test/generate-refuses-namespace-prefix.test.ts` (10 tests, 5 sequential spawns of `bin/run-dev.js` via tsx) pins, in `runMetadataGeneration` (`packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts`): the legacy `NS__SHORT` residual refusal (`os g object order__line` under `my_app`: exit 1, stdout contains `order__line` and the exact string `validateObjectNamespacePrefix('my_app_order__line','my_app')` returns, guarded `not.toBeNull()` so a gate that stopped refusing cannot make it vacuous; file list of `src/objects` and barrel bytes equal to the pre-spawn snapshot; no `Created`), and the load-failed refusal (a project whose config `defineStack` refuses the pre-fix unprefixed `legacy` object: exit 1, stdout names `objectstack.config.ts` and `'legacy'`, no `src/objects/customer.object.ts`, file list unchanged, barrel byte-identical). Correct.
- **Collected per-PR, not nightly.** `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` builds `INTEGRATION_FILES = integrationTestFiles(__dirname)` and `UNIT_FILES` from `vitest-tiers.ts`; `testFilesOnDisk` runs `selectTierFiles(files, readTierMode())` (`scripts/nightly-tiers.mjs`), which in `queue` mode (CI sets `OS_TEST_TIERS: queue`, `ci.yml:663`) keeps every file NOT matching `\.(e2e|live)\.(test|spec)\.ts$`. The new file's name has no tier suffix, and `isIntegration` fires on `childProcess` (imports `execFile` from `node:child_process`) plus `entryBasename` (`run-dev.js`) and `tsxBin` (`.bin/tsx`), so it lands in the `integration` project's exact-path `include`. `@objectstack/cli` `test` is `vitest run` (no `--project`), so both projects run. Correct.
- **Disarming reddens the file.** Residual branch removed: `objectNameFor('order__line','my_app')` yields `my_app_order__line`, charset/parse/alias checks admit it, the file and barrel line are written, so `exits 1`, the verdict assertion and `writes nothing` all fail; the namespaced control then fails as a cascade (its config now imports a legacy-form object). Load-failed branch removed (namespace read as absent): `customer.object.ts` is written with `name: 'customer'` and the barrel is appended, so all four load-failed assertions fail. Matches the PR's ablation counts (4/6 each leg). Correct.
- **Non-vacuous.** `namespacedBarrel`/`brokenBarrel` and the file lists are read from the projects `writeProject` wrote, before any spawn; the post-refusal snapshots are taken before the controls run. `customer.object.ts` under `src/objects` is the object generator's `defaultDir` plus `metadataFileName` shape (the control's `order_line.object.ts` assertion passed in CI on the same shape). The controls (`os g object order_line` writes `my_app_order_line`, prints it, updates the barrel; `os g dashboard sales` succeeds in the broken project) rule out a command that refuses everything. Correct. Two assertions add no independent guard: `residualAfter.views === false` is true by construction (`--dry-run` never writes), and the view `--dry-run` case is satisfied under the residual-disarmed leg by the load-failed cascade. The three residual assertions plus the control carry the pin; a nit, not a gap.
- **Unit file additions.** `objectTemplate.generate('sys_probe', NS)` contains `name: 'sys_probe',` (gate exempts `sys_*` in `packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts`), and `generate(NS, NS)` contains `name: 'my_app_my_app',` (`my_app` does not start with `my_app_`). Both read off the template output (`name: '${objectNameFor(name, namespace)}',`). 17 + 2 = 19 tests. Correct.
- **`cli.mdx` nits.** "`objectstack.config.ts`, `.js` or `.mjs`, the same files `os validate` auto-detects" equals `CONFIG_FILE_CANDIDATES` in `packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts`, which `findConfigPath` iterates and `resolveConfigPath` calls. "`sys_*` name is exempt ... not prefixed" and "legacy `<namespace>__<name>` form (`order__line`) is refused" match `validateObjectNamespacePrefix` (`startsWith('sys_')` returns null; `includes('__')` returns the legacy message) and the residual branch. "What it does" step 1 names the same three candidates. Correct.
- **PR body Clause-② paragraph.** Both narrowings are named in `.changeset/20197-generate-object-namespace-prefix.md` ("legacy `NS__SHORT` form ... refused before anything is written"; "config exists but does not load ... refused and nothing is written"); the legacy file was already refused by `validateNamespacePrefix` in `defineStack`; precedent `.changeset/15293-non-array-packages-refusal.md` is `patch` with `Clause-②: no` for a refusal moved earlier. True. One overstatement: "a project every other command already refuses" holds for the config-loading commands only (`os init`, `os g dashboard|skill` never load a config).
- **Merge of `origin/main` (`603aa3c0b`).** `git diff 0bd11261 018fbb2f` and `git diff 585c9af58 603aa3c0b` are byte-identical, so the merge changed none of the PR's files; main brought nothing under `packages/cli`; its only touch on a PR input is a docblock in `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` (no behaviour). `packages/lint` filter-token changes ride under `runAuthoringRules`, which the unit file calls, and CI on the merged tree is green. No new src change in the delta (`packages/cli/src` diff is empty).
- **Pre-existing wording carried into the refusal, not this PR's.** The gate's own prescription for `my_app_order__line` is `Rename it to 'my_app_line'` (drops the `order` segment); the CLI quotes it verbatim per the "gate's own words" design. Spec is read-only for this card.

### ② Semver level

`patch` + `Clause-②: no` stands. The delta adds one test file, two unit cases and doc prose; no source file changes between `018fbb2f` and `077b4c245`, so the accept set is exactly what the earlier review graded: no widening, two narrowings already refused downstream, no exported surface (`findConfigPath`/`readProjectNamespace` stay internal). Bug fix in a released package takes `patch` (Post-Task Checklist step 3).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Test-tier placement:** resolved; the per-PR integration project collects the new pin (derivation above). The nightly `.e2e` file is unchanged and still nightly.
- **PR body claims:** patch-round paragraph verified against head (file names, 10 tests / 5 spawns, both refusal facts, controls, 19 unit tests, docs). Ablation figures and local tier counts not re-run; consistent with the code reading. "every other command already refuses" is the one overstatement.
- **Governance:** file list is 8 paths, none governed; same-repo head; draft.
- **CI on `077b4c245`** (check-runs API, second poll): 42 runs, 38 success, 4 skipped (Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in, and the 11:10 re-triggered Auto Label and Check PR Size), 0 failure, 0 in progress. All seven required contexts success: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. Test Core's per-package output goes to an uploaded log artifact (blob storage, unreachable from here), so the file's presence in the CI run is derived from the config, not read from a log.
